messages:
incident-bot: Paging: potential provisioning degradation detected — increased image pull failures from external registries (dockerhub/nvcr) impacting node launch since ~10:42 UTC :rotating_light:
Maya R (oncall): seeing spikes in node boot failures, roughly 15% of new nodes failing on pull with 429/401/manifest errors.
Alex K: logs show two classes: rate-limited 429 from Docker Hub and token 401 from NVCR for a subset of instances. grabbing sample logs.
Leo T: can confirm. sample output from node bootstrap:
```
ERROR: failed to pull image registry-1.docker.io/redwood/runtime:cuda-12.1: received 429 Too Many Requests
Error response from daemon: unauthorized: authentication required
```
Tara (infra): quick check — our mirror cache hit-rate is low for the CUDA images. cache not populated for new variants. Looks like we never mirrored recent nvcr tags.
Maya R (oncall): initial impact assessment: autoscaling affected, warm pools still fine but new nodes for scaling apps and Dedicated pools are failing to provision. Customer-facing error rate up ~3% for host-level scheduling.
Priya (CS): hearing from 2 enterprise customers about increased latency and failed inference pods. They flagged queueing/backpressure.
Alex K: mitigation options: (1) enable our internal artifact proxy to fallback to cached images where present, (2) trigger a temporary mirror of specific nvcr/dockerhub tags to our internal registry, (3) fall back to older compatible images without CUDA 12.1 — but need verification.
Tara (infra): I'll try (1) now — flip artifact-proxy fallback flag to true for provisioning service. command: `./infra/ctl registry --enable-proxy-fallback`
deploy-bot: Action queued: infra/registry fallback toggled by Tara at 10:55 UTC.
Maya R (oncall): after toggle, provisioning failures dropped from 15% -> ~6% in last 3 minutes. still seeing 401s for NVCR auth renewals.
Leo T: root cause hypothesis: NVCR token provider is intermittently returning 401s due to upstream auth rate-limit or session size. Docker Hub is imposing stricter anonymous pull limits for certain CUDA layers.
Alex K: starting targeted mirror job for the hotlist images (cuda-12.1 runtime, base-libs v2). ETA ~25 min to push to our internal registry. I'll kick it off and post manifest.
Tara (infra): creating temporary provisioning policy: prefer internal-registry images, allow older image variants with `compat-cuda=11.8` for non-GPU-critical pools. Applying canary to staging then prod scaling groups.
Maya R (oncall): notifying product + CS: Priya, can you send a short customer note: "Provisioning delays for new capacity; existing workloads unaffected. Engineers applying fallbacks and mirroring; ETA ~30m." Keep it brief.
Priya (CS): drafted and sent to affected accounts at 11:05 UTC. will escalate if any SLA risk.
Alex K: mirror job started 11:07 UTC. logs: `mirror: pulling registry-1.docker.io/redwood/runtime:cuda-12.1 -> pushing internal-registry.redwood/cached/runtime:cuda-12.1`
Maya R (oncall): oncall handoff note — leaving primary to Leo in 20m. tagging for followups.
Leo T: I'll take primary. investigating NVCR token path; adding additional retry/wait in token-renewer to backoff more aggressively. also opening a support case with NVIDIA registry (ticket: NVCR-78312) and Docker Hub (ticket: DH-22944).
Tara (infra): can we protect future scale events? proposing: (a) pre-warm internal cache with top 50 images during peak, (b) increase token cache TTL with better refresh jitter, (c) telemetry to count external 429s/401s per minute.
Alex K: mirror completed at 11:28 UTC for the first set. early results: provisioning failure rate down to ~1%. rolling out new provisioning policy now.
Maya R (oncall): marking incident as partial mitigation in timeline. continuing to monitor for recurrence.
Priya (CS): customers acknowledge the update, some want postmortem.
Leo T: next steps: continue vendor engagement, add automated mirror run for critical image sets, and add a runbook step for enabling artifact-proxy fallback. I'll file a follow-up engineering ticket with action items.
Alex K: adding quick diagnostic command to run during future pages:
```
# check recent pull error types
kubectl logs -l app=provisioner -n infra --tail=200 | grep -E "429|401|manifest" | head -n 50
```
deploy-bot: Handoff note: Maya -> Leo at 11:25 UTC recorded.
Maya R (oncall): dropping from channel. Leo, please ping if you need a second pair.
Leo T: will do. marking incident status: mitigated->monitoring. collecting artifacts for postmortem.
Priya (CS): preparing customer-impact summary: affected customers: 4 Dedicated tenants, 12 small teams on autoscale. Impact window: ~10:42-11:28 UTC. Loss: delayed capacity, no data loss.
Tara (infra): creating follow-up infra ticket: INFRA-5733 "Mirror strategy & token TTL improvements". assigning to Alex and infra team.
Alex K: posted preliminary root-cause notes. Will coordinate postmortem write-up. thanks team :heart:
